ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same code with w_i set to 1 and a_i set to the uniform batch marginal, so Sinkhorn runs with isotropic Lorentz cost and no transition information; present behind a flag and never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: behaviour-scaled Lorentz cost, behaviour-mass row marginal, Sinkhorn plan, Mobius residual, one training run on the frozen budget with no early stopping and no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same code with C_ik = ||z_i^l - u_lk||^2 Euclidean, entropic scale the Euclidean batch median, and the residual chain as plain linear subtraction; present behind a flag and never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training-split sequences only, counting adjacent directed pairs (item at position t to item at t+1) into N_ij, row-normalising to P_ij, and forming m_i from the column sums of N; both become fixed length-24556 tensors gathered by item id during training.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions of the training split, summarised as successor concentration w_i (row-max of the row-normalised transition matrix) and behaviour mass m_i (add-one successor in-degree, batch-normalised).
ideas.cost_estimate: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch = about 1023 items per step, Kc = 256 codes per level, L = 3, 20 Sinkhorn iterations, latent dim about 32) each step adds one 1023x256 Lorentz cost matrix per level (about 26 MFLOP and 0.8 M arccosh) and about 31 M exponentials plus 120 reductions for Sinkhorn: roughly 3-6 ms on one modern GPU against a 20-60 ms baseline step, i.e. 5-15 percent step overhead, about 4-7 minutes of extra GPU time over all 72000 steps of 3000 epochs, with about 2 MB transient memory per level. The one-off precompute is a single sparse counting pass over the training sequences plus one encoder pass at epoch 0 to fix R; no per-epoch precompute and no SVD.
ideas.coupling_equation: C_ik = w_i * d_L(x_i, e_lk)^2 with row marginal a_i = m_i / sum_batch(m) and column marginal r = 1/Kc; plan gamma = diag(u) exp(-C/eps) diag(v), eps = median(C); residual z^{l+1} = log_0( exp_0(z^l) (+) (- exp_0(u_{l k*})) ).
ideas.coupling_path: Behaviour tensors (w_i, m_i) enter the transport-cost row scale and the row marginal of the Sinkhorn plan; the plan's row-conditional weights assign the item to hyperboloid codes and the plan's hard argmax code is Mobius-subtracted from the item's Poincare point to give the next-level residual, which is re-costed by the same behaviour-scaled Lorentz distance at the next level; removing w_i and m_i (uniform marginals, unit scale) or replacing the Lorentz cost and Mobius residual by Euclidean ones changes the plan, the codes and every downstream residual, so both factors are load-bearing in one computation.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the coupling is real, the level-1 plan is measurably sharper for high-successor-concentration items than for branching items (row entropy of gamma monotonically decreasing across w_i deciles), code usage stays near log(Kc) because of the uniform column marginal, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065, with the level-1 token alone narrowing the candidate set far below the catalogue.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantisation, at every RQ level: the Lorentz distance defines the transport cost of the assignment plan and the Mobius subtraction defines the residual the next level receives; both act in the Stage-2 forward/backward pass and therefore shape the SID tokens consumed later.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared Lorentz geodesic distance on the hyperboloid of constant curvature -c, c = 1/R^2 with R the epoch-0 median latent norm, used as optimal-transport cost; plus Mobius addition with additive inverse in the Poincare ball of the same curvature for the residual chain, and the exp/log maps at the origin between tangent space and hyperboloid/ball.
ideas.key_change: The per-level softmax/nearest-neighbour assignment becomes a 20-iteration log-domain Sinkhorn plan over a behaviour-mass marginal and a successor-concentration-scaled Lorentz cost, and the residual handed to the next level is the Mobius difference between the item's Poincare point and the chosen code's Poincare point instead of a linear subtraction.
ideas.leakage_boundary: N_ij and m_i are built exclusively from training-split sequences; the SID codebooks are fitted with those fixed tensors and neither validation nor test sequences are read at any point of SID construction, so no evaluation interaction can reach the codebooks, the marginals or the residual chain.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE Semantic IDs are fitted by Euclidean nearest neighbour with a uniform softmax, so every training item counts the same and no transition structure enters the assignment. Coarse level-1 prefixes drift towards content-similar but behaviourally unrelated items, codes no user ever traverses keep receiving gradient, and the Stage-3 generator spends its small prefix vocabulary on catalogue regions that carry almost no training traffic.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds here moved the codebook centroids (successor-weighted Frechet means), the per-level curvature (prefix transition score), or the item radius (context entropy). This proposal moves none of those: it replaces the ASSIGNMENT OPERATOR of every RQ level with an entropic optimal-transport plan whose row marginals are training-transition masses and whose row temperature is the item's successor concentration, while the transport cost is the squared Lorentz geodesic distance on a hyperboloid whose negative curvature is measured from the data. The entropic scale is the batch median transport cost, so no constant is swept. Nesting comes from a Mobius-subtraction residual chain, so behaviour mass flows from the coarse prefix down to the fine levels.
ideas.observables: Monotone decrease of level-1 mean row entropy of gamma across w_i deciles; per-level code-usage entropy staying near log(Kc) under the uniform column marginal; the behavioural diagnostics (SID coherence, transition adjacency rate, prefix transfer predictability) recorded only; per-level residual norms after Mobius subtraction; Stage-3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: Sinkhorn divergence or NaN on degenerate rows; straight-through argmax disagreeing with the soft plan and starving the decoder of coherent codes; popularity-mass marginals concentrating the codebook on head items and hurting tail SIDs; the measured curvature R making the ball too flat so the Lorentz cost is nearly Euclidean; over-soft assignment delaying convergence inside the fixed 3000 epochs; the changed plan effectively altering the codebook learning-rate behaviour
ideas.safeguards: Clamp the Lorentz arccosh argument to at least 1+1e-7 and at most 1e18; run Sinkhorn fully in log domain with logsumexp stabilisation, stop early at max row-marginal deviation 1e-3 else 20 iterations, and fall back to the hard nearest code if any output is non-finite; clamp the Poincare norm to 1/sqrt(c) - 1e-5 before every exp/log and Mobius operation; use eps = median cost plus a floor of 1e-6 times the mean cost so a degenerate batch cannot divide by zero; gather m_i and w_i with an add-one floor so unseen or successor-less items get the documented fallback (uniform marginal, w = mean w); apply the straight-through estimator so the discrete SID seen by the decoder is always a real code; log per-step Sinkhorn residual, plan entropy and residual norm, and fall back to nearest-neighbour for that step only if the plan has negative entries beyond 1e-6; all constants are the measured curvature scale R, the median-cost entropic scale, the add-one floor and the 20-iteration cap, all documented defaults, none swept.
ideas.spec_equations: N_ij from adjacent training transitions; P_ij = N_ij / sum_j' N_ij'; w_i = max_j P_ij; m_i = (sum_j N_ji + 1)/sum_i'(sum_j N_ji' + 1); c = 1/R^2, R = median_i ||z_i||_2 at epoch 0 frozen; E(u) = (cosh(sqrt(c)||u||), sinh(sqrt(c)||u||) u/(sqrt(c)||u||)); <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + sum_j x_j y_j; d_L(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) arccosh(clamp(-c<x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf)); C_ik = w_i d_L(x_i, E(u_lk))^2; eps = sg(median_ik C_ik); L_sink(u,v) = sum_ik exp(-C_ik/eps + u_i + v_k) - sum_i a_i u_i - sum_k r_k v_k with 20 alternating exact minimisations in log domain; gamma_ik = exp(-C_ik/eps + u_i + v_k); cbar_i = sum_k gamma_ik u_lk / sum_k' gamma_ik'; k*_i = argmax_k gamma_ik; p = (tanh(sqrt(c)||v||/2)/||v||) v; log_0(p) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||p||) p/||p||; p (+) q = ((1 + 2c p.q + c||q||^2) p + (1 - c||p||^2) q) / (1 + 2c p.q + c^2 ||p||^2 ||q||^2); z^{l+1} = log_0( p(z^l) (+) (-p(u_{l k*})) ).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latent z_i, trainable code tangent vectors u_lk of level l, frozen per-item scalars w_i and m_i, measured R, flags behaviour_on and geometry_on. Outputs: row-conditional plan gamma_i, soft code cbar_i for the loss, hard code indices k*_i for the discrete SID token and decoder, and the next-level residual z_i^{l+1}.

specification.text: Offline (training sequences only): N_ij = count of directed adjacent transitions i->j; P_ij = N_ij / sum_j' N_ij'; behaviour mass m_i = (indegree_i + 1) / sum_i' (indegree_i' + 1); successor concentration w_i = max_j P_ij (fallback: mean w over items with a successor). Geometry: R = median_i ||z_i||_2 measured once from the frozen initial encoder at epoch 0, c = 1/R^2, frozen. Codes are trainable tangent vectors u_lk with hyperboloid points E(u) = (cosh(sqrt(c)||u||), sinh(sqrt(c)||u||) u/(sqrt(c)||u||)). Per step, per level l = 1..L: x_i = E(z_i^l), z_i^1 = encoder output; C_ik = w_i * d_L(x_i, E(u_lk))^2 with d_L(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) arccosh(clamp(-c<x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf)); eps = stopgrad(median_ik C_ik); K_ik = exp(-C_ik/eps); log-domain Sinkhorn, 20 iterations, marginals a = m/sum_batch(m) and r = 1/Kc; row-conditional plan gamma_ik; soft code cbar_i = sum_k gamma_ik u_lk / sum_k' gamma_ik'; hard code k*_i = argmax_k gamma_ik straight-through to decoder and SID token; baseline RQ losses unchanged with cbar_i; curved residual p_i = tanh(sqrt(c)||z_i^l||/2) z_i^l/||z_i^l||, p'_i = p_i (+) (-q_i) with q_i the chosen code's Poincare point, z_i^{l+1} = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||p'_i||) p'_i/||p'_i||.

ideas.title: Behaviour-marginal Lorentzian optimal-transport quantization of the RQ-VAE SID prefix hierarchy

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: m_p and the successor multiset replaced by the prefix's own item count and its own items, i.e. w_j = 1 for j in S_p, so the allocation sees no transitions. Exists in code behind BEHAVIOUR_ON=False, is unit-checked, is computed once as a static diagnostic and is never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single trained configuration: transition weights AND Lorentz curvature K=-1/s^2 spread both active, producing N_p and the slice-restricted level assignments. One training run, 3000 Stage 2 epochs, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no tuning sweep, no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: BEHAVIOUR_ON=True but K set to 0 in the allocation branch, so the Frechet mean becomes the weighted Euclidean mean and sigma_p the weighted Euclidean standard deviation, giving a different N_p. Exists behind GEOMETRY_ON=False, unit-checked, static diagnostic only, never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One restricted pass over Stage 2 training sequences only. For each consecutive pair (i_t, i_t+1), c[i_t, i_t+1] += 1. Rows are normalised, the top M=8 successors per item kept (documented default) and renormalised, and m_i = sum_j c_ij stored with log1p. For a prefix p, m_p = sum over i in S_p of m_i, and the successor multiset is the union of the kept rows of all i in S_p with summed weights.
ideas.behavior_signal: User-interest branching expressed as directed item transitions aggregated per SID prefix: the transition mass m_p and the successor multiset of each prefix.
ideas.cost_estimate: Negligible relative to baseline. Encoder/decoder/Stage 3 cost unchanged; the level-level argmin is the same total size (every item still scans N codewords, only within its own prefix slice). Added work is one allocation refresh every C=100 epochs: 30 refreshes over 3000 epochs, each 24556*8 = 196448 successor pairs, 5 Frechet iterations and 5 k-means iterations in ambient dim D+1 (D=32), about 1.6e7 flops per refresh and about 5e8 flops in total. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch) the added cost is one slice-offset lookup, below 0.5% wall clock; the transition matrix is built once before training.
ideas.coupling_equation: N_p = max(1, LR_round( N * (m_p * sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)) / sum_q (m_q * sigma_q^2)^(D/(D+2)) )) with sigma_p^2 = sum_j w_j d_K(m_p^*, x_j)^2 / sum_j w_j and m_p^* = argmin_x sum_j w_j d_K(x, x_j)^2, where the w_j are behaviour transition weights and d_K is the Lorentz distance of curvature K = -1/s^2.
ideas.coupling_path: training transition graph -> per-prefix behaviour mass m_p and successor multiset -> per-prefix curved spread sigma_p around the Lorentz Frechet mean -> derived slot count N_p -> the prefix's codebook slice and its offsets -> slice-restricted argmin -> level-l SID token -> Stage 3 prompt tokens. Removing behaviour makes m_p and the successor multiset uninformative (uniform allocation); removing curvature changes the mean and spread (Euclidean variance gives a different N_p); either change moves the argmin and hence the emitted token.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If capacity follows behaviour branching in curved latent space, then high-mass/high-spread prefixes receive visibly more level-2 slots (spread of N_p across prefixes clearly above 1), the fraction of training transitions whose successor shares the item's level-2 prefix rises, and Stage 3 test recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single both-on run; if N_p is nearly uniform and recall stays at or below 0.065, the idea is discarded.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In quantization capacity allocation: at every C-th epoch boundary, inside the RQ-VAE codebook-budget schedule, before the level-l slice-restricted nearest-codeword assignment and the matching k-means slice rebuild.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz model of constant negative curvature K = -1/s^2 with radius s = median training latent norm measured once at initialisation (a measured scale, not tuned). Operations: exp_0^K, the Lorentz distance d_K(a,b) = s*arccosh(-<a,b>_L/s^2) with signature (-,+), and a weighted Riemannian (Karcher) Frechet mean computed by fixed-step gradient descent.
ideas.key_change: At every level l>=2 the total slot budget N is split across prefixes by the high-rate quantization rule N_p proportional to (m_p * sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)), where m_p is the training transition mass leaving the prefix and sigma_p is the hyperbolic (Lorentz) Frechet spread of that prefix's training successors; the level-l assignment argmin is then restricted to prefix p's own slice of N_p codewords.
ideas.leakage_boundary: W, m_p, the successor multisets and the median norm scale s come exclusively from the training-split sequences, and sigma_p from encoder latents of training items. Validation and test sequences are never read during SID construction, allocation or codebook refresh, and the item catalogue is the frozen training catalogue, so no validation or test interaction can enter a SID token.
ideas.motivation: An RQ-VAE SID gives every first-level prefix exactly the same number of child codewords. User behaviour is not uniform: a few prefixes are transition hubs whose continuations fan out broadly, while many prefixes lead to a narrow, almost deterministic next item. Uniform fanout spends most of the second/third-level capacity on prefixes with almost no future traffic and starves the hubs, so quantization error concentrates exactly where the generative recommender samples next tokens most often.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds kept the fanout schedule fixed and changed codebook update weights (Poincare-Frechet successors), per-level curvature (CURVCTRL-SID), per-item radius (BRad-RQ), Lorentz profile smoothing, behaviour cones, geodesic shifts or branch-curvature MoE. Here the structure of the code changes: the per-prefix code budget N_p is a derived quantity and each prefix owns a disjoint contiguous slice of the level codebook, so prefixes get unequal numbers of SID children. Nothing in the repository allocates codebook capacity, and nothing derives a capacity from a hyperbolic spread of successors.
ideas.observables: Distribution (min/median/max and entropy) of N_p at levels 2 and 3; per-level code usage entropy; successor prefix predictability, i.e. the fraction of training transitions whose successor shares the source item's level-1 and level-2 prefix; SID collision count and prefix counts; the allocation computed statically for the behaviour-off and geometry-off configurations without any extra training; and Stage 3 test_recall@10.
risks: sigma_p may be nearly constant across prefixes, so the both-on allocation collapses to the uniform schedule and the run degenerates into a baseline run.; Capacity concentration can starve low-mass prefixes and raise collisions for long-tail next-item targets.; The C=100 warm-start reallocation could oscillate and destabilise the EMA codebooks.; The exponent D/(D+2) close to 1 makes the allocation nearly proportional to mass, so the geometric term may be too weak to change any argmin.; The generative recommender's per-level vocabulary becomes level-dependent in size, which requires a careful deterministic token-space remap.; Behaviour mass is dominated by popular items, so the allocation may simply reproduce a popularity prior at the SID level.
ideas.safeguards: sigma_p clipped to measured q05/q95 quantiles of the same epoch so no degenerate prefix owns the whole budget; N_p floored at 1 and capped at N-(P-1) so every prefix keeps at least one child; largest-remainder rounding guarantees sum N_p = N exactly; cosh and arccosh arguments clamped (>= 1 + 1e-7) and norm denominators floored at 1e-8; the Frechet gradient step is capped at radius s so no exp map leaves the chart; allocation refreshes happen only at epoch boundaries with warm-started k-means so the EMA codebooks cannot oscillate; the transition graph is frozen before training so no validation/test interaction can leak in; the level token vocabulary is remapped deterministically from the global slot index so the generative recommender sees a stable token space.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) c_ij = count of consecutive (i,j) in training sequences; W_ij = c_ij / sum_j' c_ij', top-M=8 kept and renormalised; m_i = sum_j c_ij. (2) s = median_i ||mu_i||_2 at init; K = -1/s^2; x_i = exp_0^K(mu_i). (3) d_K(a,b) = s*arccosh(-<a,b>_L/s^2). (4) Per prefix p with aggregated weights w_j and mass m_p = sum_j w_j: x_p^(0) = exp_0^K( sum_j w_j mu_j / m_p ); for t=0..4: g = -2 sum_j w_j log_{x_p^(t)}(x_j) / m_p and x_p^(t+1) = exp_{x_p^(t)}(eta_t g) with eta_t = s/(2 sqrt(t+1)); m_p^* = x_p^(5). (5) sigma_p^2 = sum_j w_j d_K(m_p^*, x_j)^2 / m_p, with sigma_p clipped to the measured [q05,q95] quantiles over the same epoch's prefixes. (6) alpha = D/(D+2); a_p = (m_p sigma_p^2)^alpha; N_p = max(1, floor(N a_p / sum a_p)) with the deficit distributed by largest remainder so sum_p N_p = N exactly. (7) o_p = cumulative sum of N_p; level-l assignment for item i with prefix p: k_l(i) = argmin_{k in [o_p, o_p + N_p)} || r_l(i) - C_l[k] ||_2^2, with the slice initialised by 5-step warm-started k-means on the residuals of S_p and then EMA-updated as in the baseline. (8) Refresh at epoch boundaries only, every C = 100 epochs, 30 refreshes in total.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only transition counts, the EMA latent table over 24556 items, the prefix assignment from the previous epoch, the level slot budget N, the residual dimension D and the measured scale s. Outputs: integer per-prefix slot counts N_p, contiguous slice offsets o_p, per-prefix initialised codebook rows, and the slice-restricted codeword indices that become the SID tokens.

specification.text: Build W (top-M row-normalised directed transition counts) and m_p from training sequences only; measure s = median latent norm at init and fix K = -1/s^2; at every C epochs map the EMA latent table to the Lorentz model, compute for each prefix p the weighted Riemannian Frechet mean and spread with 5 fixed gradient steps, allocate N_p by largest-remainder rounding of (m_p sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)) with integer floor 1 and clipping of sigma_p to measured q05/q95, rebuild each prefix's codebook slice by 5-step warm-started k-means, and keep the standard EMA codeword update between refreshes.

ideas.title: Behaviour-branching hyperbolic capacity allocation: the number of SID slots each prefix subtree owns is derived from training transition mass and hyperbolic successor spread

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: m_i = 0 for every item (successor matrix zeroed at load time), with Lorentz distances, the measured caps s_l, the codebook and all other heads unchanged, so eta = 0, the step is exactly the identity and the run is the hyperbolic RQ baseline.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run described here, trained once on the frozen budget with no early stopping and no other arm run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp_r(eta*u) replaced by the tangent-space linear step r + eta*u and d_L replaced by the Euclidean distance, while eta and u keep their full behaviour dependence, so behaviour still steers but curvature is gone.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-1/2 training interaction sequences only: build the sparse count matrix N with n_ij = number of training sessions in which item j is the successor of item i (window 1); normalise rows to p_ij = n_ij / sum_j n_ij; with the frozen pre-Stage-2 content embeddings Z (n_items x d) compute b_i = sum_j p_ij (z_j - z_i), u_i = PT_{o->x_i}([0, b_i]) (a Lorentz tangent vector at the item's lifted point), and m_i = (n_(1) - n_(2)) / (n_(1) + n_(2)) from the two largest outgoing counts (n_(2) = 0 if the item has one successor; m_i = 0 if the item has no training successor). Computed once before Stage 2 and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions of the training split, summarised per item as a unit successor direction plus a transition concentration (top-2 margin); both are training-only.
ideas.cost_estimate: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs, batch 256, M=256 codes, d=64, L=3): extra per step is ~3*256 tangent projections (64 flops each) + 2 cosh/sinh per item per level + one extra time component in the existing B*M*d code comparison, i.e. about 1.2 MFLOP, under 1% of the step's matmul cost; measured cost expectation +1% to +3% wall clock. One-off: sparse successor aggregate (nnz ~ 20*24556 times d ~ 31 MFLOP) and one 4096-item median per level at initialisation, i.e. seconds. No extra encoder forward pass, no extra parameters, no extra memory beyond three (n_items x d) frozen matrices.
ideas.coupling_equation: r~_i^(l) = exp_{r_i^(l-1)}( m_i * min(rho_i, s_l) * u_i^(l) ), k_l = argmin_k d_L(r~_i^(l), c_k), with rho_i = arcosh(<x_i, e_0>_L) the radial depth of the item latent and u_i^(l) the behaviour successor direction orthogonalised against the current query.
ideas.coupling_path:
residual query r_(l-1) -> behaviour tangent u_i and rapidity eta_i^(l) = m_i * min(rho_i, s_l) -> hyperbolic exponenti

al step r~ = exp_r(eta*u) -> Lorentz nearest-code argmin -> code k_l -> SID token l -> and (via the unstepped query) the Euclidean residual that feeds level l+1, plus the straight-through gradient into the encoder. Removing behaviour (m_i = 0) makes the step the identity and the pathway becomes plain hyperbolic RQ; removing curvature (Euclidean addition and Euclidean distance) changes both the step and the argmin. Neither term is decoration: each changes the computed code sequence.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis:
Behaviour steering of code assignment is only worth keeping i

f it re-assigns prefixes without destroying reconstruction. It must therefore be true that level-1 and level-2 code usage entropy stay within roughly 10% of the behaviour-off value and per-level reconstruction loss degrades by less than roughly 10% relative, while the behaviour-alignment diagnostic (share of items whose top successor sits in the same level-1 code) rises clearly above its behaviour-off value and Stage3 test_recall@10 lands above 0.065. If reconstruction degrades much more than that, the step is damaging cells rather than steering them and recall should not improve; that single run decides it.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the Stage-2 residual quantizer, at the assignment step of every RQ level, applied to the residual query immediately before the nearest-code search; through the straight-through estimator it also acts on the gradient that reaches the RQ-VAE encoder.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed unit negative curvature (kappa = 1) Lorentz hyperboloid; the operator is the exponential map exp_r(eta*u) = r*cosh(eta) + u*sinh(eta) along a unit tangent u at r (a geodesic translation, an isometry of the hyperboloid), and code selection uses the geodesic distance in the stable form d_L(a,b) = 2*asinh(||a-b||_M / 2).
ideas.key_change: At each RQ level l the query is replaced by r~ = exp_r(eta_i^(l) * u_i^(l)), one geodesic step of length eta in the tangent direction that points at the item's training-successor aggregate; codes are then chosen by Lorentz geodesic distance, while the residual carried to level l+1 is taken from the unstepped query so the reconstruction scale is unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: N is counted only over training sequences; Z is the frozen content embedding of training items plus item metadata; u_i, m_i and s_l are functions of those and of training items only. No validation or test interaction, and no validation-derived statistic, enters the SID construction. Validation/test quantities appear only in post-hoc diagnostics and Stage 3 scoring, never in the operator, the codebook or the cap.
ideas.motivation: A generative recommender decodes SID prefixes autoregressively from the user history, so what makes the early tokens useful is the direction in which an item's code deviates from its content neighbours toward the items users actually go to next. A content-only RQ-VAE spends all of its levels on reconstruction, so level-1 and level-2 inclusive prefixes under-determine the next item and Stage 3 recall stalls near the baseline. Items that share a successor distribution should share a prefix; nothing in a plain Euclidean RQ-VAE enforces that.
ideas.novelty: Distinct from every mechanism already tried in this programme: it is not a successor-weighted Fréchet codebook refit (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), not a per-level curvature field driven by prefix-transition scores (CURVCTRL-SID), not a radial ranking of codes by context entropy (BRad-RQ), not successor-profile smoothing, behaviour cones, branching-curvature MoE or a successor shift of the embedding. The codebook, the curvature, the losses and the level structure are all untouched. The single new object is an isometric exponential-map step inserted into the residual-query recursion: because it is a Lorentz isometry it preserves the query's hyperbolic norm, so it steers code assignment without inflating the reconstruction residual (a shift cannot do this), and because it is applied before every level's nearest-code search the behaviour signal recurses through the whole prefix hierarchy instead of touching one level. Its rapidity is a product of two measured quantities (transition top-2 margin, hyperbolic radial depth) capped by a measured quantization scale, so no constant is tuned.
ideas.observables: level-wise code usage entropy; behaviour-alignment rate (fraction of items whose most frequent training successor shares the level-1 code) as a diagnostic; held-out prefix-transition log-likelihood as a diagnostic; the ratio of encoder gradient norms for high-margin versus zero-margin items (should scale like cosh(eta)); per-level reconstruction loss; Stage3 test_recall@10 as the only judgement.
risks: ["The step could rotate queries out of their own cell, raising reconstruction loss and starving rarely used codes, which would cost recall instead of gaining it.", "If successor directions are noisy (sparse transitions), m_i is near zero for most items and the mechanism silently reduces to the plain hyperbolic RQ baseline, i.e. no effect.", "With only 3000 epochs on four cards one run cannot separate a real gain from seed noise, so the effect size must be large enough to be visible in a single run.", "Applying the step before every level could compound displacements so that deep levels encode behaviour direction instead of residual content, hurting fine reconstruction.", "The measured cell radius s_l is fixed after initialisation, so a codebook that moves a lot during training may leave the cap mismatched to the current cell size."]
ideas.safeguards:
clamp eta to [0, s_l] and floor s_l at 1e-3; if ||b_i|| < 1e-8 or the item has no training successor set m_i = 0 and eta = 0 (exact identity, cold items fall back to plain RQ); compute d_L in the

2*asinh(||a-b||_M/2) form and clamp the arcosh argument used for rho_i to at least 1+1e-7 to avoid NaN gradients; normalise u_hat with the closed-form 1/sqrt(1+a^2) so it stays a unit tangent up to float error; use -<r~,c_k>_L for the argmin (no arcosh in the hot loop) and score-tie-break by the smaller code index for determinism; guard cosh/sinh against overflow by the eta <= s_l clip (s_l is a median of small geodesic lengths, so eta stays O(1)); keep the behaviour statistics in float32 outside the autograd graph and freeze the successor matrix after the one-off build; rebuild nothing from validation data; log level-wise usage entropy every epoch so a collapsed level is visible.
ideas.spec_equations: Let x = exp_o([0, z]) = (cosh rho, sinh rho * zhat), rho = ||z||, zhat = z/rho, e_0 = (1,0), <a,b>_L = -a_0 b_0 + a.b. SID levels l = 1..L with Lorentz codes c_k = exp_o([0, w_k]). Residual stream v_0 = z, query r_l = exp_o(v_l). For each level: (1) transport the frozen successor direction u_i from x_i to the query: u <- PT(r_l) and project, u_perp = u + <u, r_l>_L * r_l, u_hat = u_perp / sqrt(1 + <u, r_l>_L^2); (2) eta_i^(l) = m_i * min(rho_i, s_l); (3) r~ = r_l*cosh(eta) + u_hat*sinh(eta); (4) k_l = argmax_k (-<r~, c_k>_L); (5) v_{l+1} = v_l - w_{k_l} (Euclidean residual from the unstepped query, so the commit/reconstruction losses are unchanged in scale); (6) SID(i) = (k_1, ..., k_L). Caps: s_l = median over a frozen 4096-item training sample at initialisation of d_L(exp_o(v_{l-1}), c_{k_l}) taken with the behaviour-off selection. All of eta, m_i, u_i, rho_i and s_l are detached from the graph (torch.no_grad for the statistics); gradients pass through exp_o, exp_o(.) and exp_r only.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the encoder output z_i (d-dim), the Lorentz codebook {c_k} kept in tangent coordinates w_k, the frozen per-item arrays u_i (d-dim tangent components) and m_i (scalar), and the measured per-level caps s_l. Outputs: the discrete code sequence k_1..k_L that becomes the item's SID tuple, the per-level Lorentz distances for the usage/entropy diagnostics, and the Euclidean residual stream for the unchanged reconstruction and commit losses.

specification.text: precompute once from training transitions -> per-item unit tangent u_i and margin m_i; measure median cell radius s_l per level at init; in every forward pass, for l=1..L: project u_i onto the tangent space at the current residual query, set eta = m_i * min(rho_i, s_l), step the query into exp_r(eta*u), pick k_l = argmax_k (-<r~, c_k>_L), emit token l, advance the Euclidean residual with the unstepped query. All eta, m, u, rho are detached; gradients flow through exp and exp_r into the encoder.

ideas.title: Behaviour-rapidity geodesic stepping of every RQ residual query, with rapidity capped by the measured quantization cell radius

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Switch BEHAV_COCON = 0 exists in the code: neighbour rows are replaced by the identity row, so the Karcher update degenerates to the item alone (z_i = v_i) while the curved quantizer stays active. Not trained in this round; it exists so the behaviour contribution is well defined.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Switches BEHAV_COCON = 1 and GEOM_CURV = 1, the single trained candidate reported as the round result: full coupling, one run, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep, no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Switch GEOM_CURV = 0 exists in the code and takes c -> 0, where log, exp and parallel transport become the identity, the Karcher mean becomes the weighted Euclidean mean of the same neighbours and d_c becomes the Euclidean distance, i.e. exactly a Euclidean RQ-VAE with the same behaviour graph. Not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage 1 and Stage 2 training sequences only. For each training sequence count every unordered item pair present (no time-window constant is introduced: the whole training sequence of a user defines co-consumption). n_i, n_j are the numbers of training sequences containing the item and N the number of training sequences; pmi_ij = log(n_ij N / (n_i n_j)). Keep neighbours with pmi_ij > log 2 (lift at least 2, a rule-based significance-style threshold), rank by pmi and keep at most 16 (compute cap at 64 dims). Rows are normalised to sum to one and the self weight is fixed to 1.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted co-consumption neighbours: pointwise-mutual-information-weighted symmetric item pairs formed inside user training sequences (sequential co-consumption, popularity corrected by PMI).
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time graph build over training sequences (24556 items, at most 16 stored neighbours, about 1.6 MB). Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps per epoch, batch about 1023 items, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): about 34 log maps plus 2 exp maps for aggregation and about 9 manifold ops for the 3-level residual chain per item, roughly 45 transcendental 64-dim vector ops per item, about 46k per step, under 10 percent of a step's wall clock; total Stage 2 wall clock +8 to +15 percent, no extra epochs, no extra passes.
ideas.coupling_equation: SID_i = RQ_c(z_i), z_i = argmin_{x in B_c} sum_{j in {i} U N(i)} w_ij^behaviour * d_c(x, v_j)^2, solved as x <- exp_x^c( sum_j w_ij log_x^c(v_j) ); per level k_l = argmin_k d_c(u_l, c_{l,k}) with u_{l+1} = exp_0^c( log_{c_{l,k}}^c(u_l) / (1 - c |c_{l,k}|^2) ).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour weights -> geodesic Karcher aggregation -> z_i -> geodesic RQ assignment and transport -> SID prefix. The behaviour weights are the coefficients of the log maps defining z_i and curvature is the metric in which those log maps, the Karcher update and the code distance are computed, so dropping the edges changes z_i and dropping curvature changes the operator that both produces and quantizes z_i. There is no separate behaviour loss and no separate geometric loss.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If co-consumed items become geodesically close before quantization, they should share RQ prefixes more often and the generator should predict a prefix that transfers to unseen items, showing up as Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single coupled run, together with a lower prefix-collision rate for high-lift co-consumption pairs than the baseline Euclidean RQ-VAE records.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Both in training (inside the encoder, where the item point that will be quantized is produced, and inside the quantizer's argmin and residual chain of every RQ level, hence in the gradient reaching the encoder) and in the final SID assignment pass, which applies the same operator to all 24556 items.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c = 1 (unit curvature, the canonical scale of the ball, not tuned): Moebius log and exp maps, geodesic distance d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) |(-u) (+) v|), the Karcher mean built from log maps, and parallel transport of the level residual to the origin.
ideas.key_change: The item point becomes a 2-step geodesic Karcher mean of its own embedding and its popularity-adjusted co-consumption neighbours in the Poincare ball; the quantizer then assigns codes by geodesic distance and carries the residual to the next level by parallel transport to the origin instead of Euclidean subtraction.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Pair counts, PMI, neighbour lists and row weights are computed from the frozen training split before Stage 2 starts and are never recomputed during Stage 3 or from validation or test interactions. No validation or test item, sequence or co-occurrence is read at any point of SID construction, and the final SID assignment pass uses only item identity plus its training-derived weight row, so an unseen test interaction cannot alter a code.
ideas.motivation: An item's RQ-VAE point comes only from its own encoder row, so two items that users consume together can land in unrelated regions of the ball and receive unrelated SID prefixes; the generator then has to memorise the pairing instead of predicting a shared prefix. The defect is item-side: the point that gets quantized ignores the popularity-adjusted co-consumption neighbourhood.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms act on the codebook (successor-weighted Karcher/Frechet code mass), on the curvature schedule per RQ level (measured hard prefix-transition score) and on the item radial coordinate (transition-context entropy). None changes the aggregation OPERATOR that builds the item point, and none uses constructor co-consumption. Here negative curvature is the metric in which the behaviour neighbourhood is averaged (a Riemannian Karcher mean over Poincare log maps), and the same metric then defines the RQ residual transport, so behaviour enters as edge weights of one equation and curvature as the operator and distance in that same equation.
ideas.observables: Share rate of SID prefixes for high-lift co-consumption pairs at level 1 and level 2; the distribution of geodesic radii of item points; per-level code usage and collision counts; the commitment term expressed in geodesic distance; the prefix-transition predictability diagnostic (recorded, never gated); and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10.
risks: Long-tail items have too few lift>=2 partners, so z_i stays near v_i and the mechanism is inert exactly where SIDs matter.; Hyperbolic averaging can over-smooth and collapse distinct items onto one code, raising collisions and possibly hurting recall.; 2 Karcher iterations may leave a convergence bias that appears as inflated commitment loss and slightly shifted code usage.; If the generator already fits prefixes without item-side structure, the recall gain may sit inside single-seed noise.; The geometry-off and behaviour-off comparisons exist only as code switches, so the causal claim rests on one trained run.
ideas.safeguards: Project every ball point and every exp-map output to radius at most 0.9/sqrt(c) to bound lambda_x; clamp tangent norms to 1/sqrt(c) before exp; evaluate artanh with its argument clipped to 1 - 1e-7 and add epsilon inside all norms; add 1e-8 to counts before the PMI ratio and drop pairs with n_ij < 2 to avoid single-sequence PMI spikes; cap stored neighbours at 16 and floor-normalise rows so no single neighbour exceeds 0.9 of the row mass; break argmin ties deterministically by code index so assigned SIDs are reproducible; if a row has no kept neighbour use the self weight alone (identity fallback) so no division by zero occurs; skip the Karcher update for items already within 1e-4 of the radius clamp; log the count of items left with identity rows as a diagnostic only.
ideas.spec_equations: lambda_x = 2/(1 - c|x|^2). u (+) v = ((1 + 2c<u,v> + c|v|^2)u + (1 - c|u|^2)v) / (1 + 2c<u,v> + c^2|u|^2|v|^2). d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)|(-u)(+)v|). exp_x(v) = x (+) (tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x |v|/2) v/(sqrt(c)|v|)). log_x(y) = (2/(sqrt(c) lambda_x)) artanh(sqrt(c)|(-x)(+)y|) ((-x)(+)y)/|(-x)(+)y|. PT_{0<-c}(r) = lambda_c r / 2 = r/(1 - c|c|^2). Aggregation: a_ii = 1, a_ij = pmi_ij / sum_{j' in N(i)} pmi_ij', w_ij = a_ij / sum_j a_ij; x_0 = v_i; for t = 1,2: g_t = sum_j w_ij log_{x_{t-1}}(v_j); x_t = exp_{x_{t-1}}(g_t); z_i = x_2. Quantization: u_1 = z_i; for l = 1..L: k_l = argmin_k d_c(u_l, c_{l,k}); u_{l+1} = exp_0( log_{c_{l,k_l}}(u_l) / (1 - c|c_{l,k_l}|^2) ). Loss: L = L_recon(z_i) + beta sum_l [ d_c(u_l, c_{l,k_l})^2 + d_c(sg[u_l], c_{l,k_l})^2 ] with the baseline beta, baseline L_recon, and 3 levels x 256 codes inherited unchanged. Constants: c = 1, lift threshold log 2, k <= 16, T = 2, radius clamp 0.9/sqrt(c), all derived rules or documented defaults, none swept.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: per item the encoder embedding v_i in the ball (64 dims), the training-only row (neighbour ids, normalised PMI weights) of at most 16 entries, the level codebooks, and the fixed curvature c. Outputs: the aggregated point z_i, the L prefix code indices forming the item SID, and the geodesic commitment loss whose gradient reaches both the encoder and the codebooks.

specification.text: Build the symmetric popularity-adjusted co-consumption graph from training sequences only: pmi_ij = log(n_ij * N / (n_i n_j)), keep neighbours with pmi_ij > log 2, cap 16 by pmi, row-normalise with self weight 1. Point: x_0 = v_i; for t in 1..2 compute g = sum_j w_ij log_x(v_j) and set x = exp_x(g). Quantize z_i = x_2 with geodesic argmin per level, residual r = log_{c_l}(u_l), next query u_{l+1} = exp_0(r / (1 - c|c_l|^2)). Loss = baseline reconstruction plus commitment rewritten with squared geodesic distance. c = 1 fixed, no sweep.

ideas.title: Co-consumption graph as the hyperbolic aggregation operator: curved Karcher item points feeding a geodesic residual RQ-VAE.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Flag behaviour_anchor = False sets atilde_l := r_l at every level, so the two score terms coincide, the argmin equals the pure curved RQ ordering and the mechanism reduces to the curved baseline. The flag exists and is unit-tested on a fixed batch, but no such arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: PMI Einstein-midpoint anchors active and the Poincare metric active at every level. This is the single trained candidate.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Flag hyperbolic = False replaces exp_0/log_0/d_c by identity maps and Euclidean norms: score_k = ||r_l - e_{l,k}||^2 + ||atilde_l - e_{l,k}||^2, the anchor is the weighted Euclidean mean of neighbour embeddings and the reconstruction is a squared Euclidean error. Exists, never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training split only: for every training user sequence, deduplicate items, increment item counts n_i and unordered pair counts n_ij; p_ij proportional to n_ij, p_i proportional to n_i; PMI_ij = log(p_ij/(p_i*p_j)); keep neighbours with PMI_ij > 0, top 20 by PMI, weights w_ij proportional to PMI_ij. Computed once before Stage 2 and stored as a frozen buffer.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted co-consumption neighbours of each training item (positive-PMI top-20) and their PMI weights, condensed into one Einstein-midpoint anchor per item.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step: 2*L*K*B = 2*3*256*1024 = 1.57M curved distance evaluations (about 40 MFLOP plus ~5M tanh/artanh) plus B*L = 3072 exp_0/log_0 calls, against a transformer step of order 1e11 FLOP, i.e. expected below 3% step time and below 2% wall-clock over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps. One-off CPU preprocessing: sparse session co-occurrence over 24556 items (10^5-10^6 pair increments), top-20 neighbour lists about 4 MB, N*d anchor floats; zero recurring cost because training-split transitions are fixed.
ideas.coupling_equation: score_l(k) = d_c(exp_0^c(r_l^i), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0^c(atilde_l^i), e_{l,k})^2 with atilde_l^i = a_l^i * min(1, ||r_l^i||/||a_l^i||), r_{l+1} = r_l - u_{l,c_l}, a_{l+1} = a_l - u_{l,c_l}, a_1^i = log_0^c(EinsteinMidpoint{w_ij, p_j}), u_{l,k} = log_0^c(e_{l,k}).
ideas.coupling_path: One loop per item: the content remainder r_l and the behaviour-anchor remainder a_l are both exp-mapped into the ball and both compared to the SAME candidate code with the SAME curved metric; the winning code's tangent vector updates both remainders. The chosen code therefore depends jointly on the PMI-derived anchor and on the curvature, and removing either (anchor term or curved metric) changes the code sequence produced at every level.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If SID prefixes carry behavioural role, then items co-consumed far more than popularity predicts will share level-1 and level-2 prefixes far more often than content-only assignment allows, level-2/3 prefix conditional entropy on training sequences will fall, and the single frozen Stage-3 run will give test_recall@10 above 0.065. The idea is worthless if recall stays at or below 0.065 while the logged steering rate (share of items whose chosen code differs from the content-only argmin) exceeds 5% and the PMI prefix share rose, or if the steering rate is near zero, in which case the coupling is inert.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantization during Stage-2 training: the level-wise code selection score, the residual recursion and the reconstruction term. The codebook entries remain ball points used through the tangent chart at the origin, with unchanged count and update rule.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with fixed negative curvature c = 1: origin exponential and logarithmic maps exp_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||), log_0(p) = artanh(sqrt(c)||p||)*p/(sqrt(c)||p||), Moebius distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x) xor_c y||), and the closed-form Einstein midpoint for the anchor.
ideas.key_change: The residual chain is redefined in the tangent chart at the ball origin, the level-l code is chosen by a two-term Poincare score (content-remainder distance plus clipped behaviour-anchor-remainder distance), and the reconstruction loss becomes the Poincare distance to the exponential image of the sum of chosen code tangent vectors.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The PMI graph, the anchor tensor, the scale s and the clip ratio are all computed from training-split sequences and training-item embeddings before Stage 2 and stored read-only. No validation or test interaction enters the counts, the anchors or the SID construction; no checkpoint selection, early stopping or Stage-3 tuning touches them, and every constant is fixed before the run starts.
ideas.motivation: Content-only RQ-VAE Semantic IDs place items that play the same behavioural role in different prefix subtrees, because a co-consumed complement and its partner usually look nothing alike. The Stage-3 generative recommender then has to learn the same next-prefix distribution once per subtree and adjacent prefixes compete, so recall saturates below the 0.065 target. The aim is a prefix hierarchy that is partially role-aware while remaining content-decisive, without touching the codebook size, the curvature schedule or the frozen Stage-3 protocol.
ideas.novelty: Neither the codebook nor the curvature is changed: no Frechet/Einstein codebook update, no per-level curvature control, no radial or rank modulation, no successor-profile smoothing, no cones, no mixture-of-branches. The behaviour signal is a symmetric popularity-corrected (PMI) co-consumption graph, not the directed successor distribution used by the earlier rounds. It enters as a SECOND GEODESIC ENDPOINT inside the level-wise argmin: every level compares the same candidate code both to the current content remainder point and to the current behaviour-anchor remainder point in the same Poincare metric, and the anchor remainder is propagated with the chosen code tangent vector, so the behaviour constraint is active at levels 1..L rather than at one level or in one loss term.
ideas.observables: Steering rate per level (share of items whose chosen code differs from the content-only argmin, logged in the same run); PMI-neighbour prefix share at level 1 and level 2 of the produced SIDs; per-level code usage entropy; level-2 and level-3 prefix conditional entropy on training sequences; reconstruction Poincare error; Stage-3 test_recall@10 as the judgement.
risks: Behaviour anchors can drag items into codes that no longer decode their content, raising reconstruction error and making the SID ambiguous for the recommender.; Chain-like catalogues may compress into shared level-1 codes and inflate collisions, so the generative model cannot resolve adjacent items.; PMI counts over long sessions are noisy for rare and cold items, whose anchors are then neutral and contribute nothing.; The discrete argmin gives no direct gradient, so the encoder only feels the behaviour through reconstruction of the newly chosen code; the effect may be too weak.; A single seed may not separate a small genuine gain from seed noise near the 0.065 threshold.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ||p|| <= 0.9 and every artanh argument to 1-1e-7; eps = 1e-8 in the clip-ratio denominator and in all norms; if the Einstein-midpoint numerator norm is below eps or the item has no positive-PMI neighbour, set a_1 := r_1 so the anchor term duplicates the content term and the baseline ordering is exactly preserved; keep the anchor a detached frozen buffer so no gradient forces the encoder to satisfy behaviour; deterministic tie-break by lowest code index; no codebook reinitialisation, usage-weight or temperature sweep is introduced; all diagnostics are recorded only and never gate the run.
ideas.spec_equations: p_i = exp_0(kappa z_i), kappa = artanh(0.9)/s, s = q99(||z||); gamma_j = 1/(1-||p_j||^2); a_i = (sum_j w_ij gamma_j p_j)/||sum_j w_ij gamma_j p_j||, w_ij proportional to max(PMI_ij,0) over the top-20; a_1 = log_0(a_i); for l = 1..L: atilde = a_l * min(1, ||r_l||/max(||a_l||,1e-8)); s_k = d_c(exp_0(r_l), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0(atilde), e_{l,k})^2; c_l = argmin_k s_k (lowest index on ties); SID_i[l] = c_l; u = log_0(e_{l,c_l}); r <- r - u; a <- a - u; loss = mean_i d_c(p_i, exp_0(sum_l u_{l,c_l}))^2 + beta*mean_i ||r_1^i - sg(sum_l u_{l,c_l})||^2 with beta as in the baseline.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen training-item content embeddings z_i, training-split SID-construction session sequences for the PMI graph, an L-level x K-code codebook of ball points, and the two flags behaviour_anchor and hyperbolic. Outputs: one SID tuple (c_1..c_L) per item, the curved reconstruction loss with gradients for encoder and codebook, and a diagnostics record with steering rates, PMI prefix shares, usage entropy and per-level prefix entropy.

specification.text: Frozen training-item embeddings z_i (N=24556, dim d). Scale kappa = artanh(r_max)/(sqrt(c)*s) with s = 99th percentile of ||z_i||, r_max = 0.9, c = 1, so p_i = exp_0(kappa*z_i) and its tangent vector is r_1^i = kappa*z_i. From training-session co-occurrence build positive-PMI neighbours j of i (top k=20) with weights w_ij proportional to PMI_ij normalized to one; the behaviour anchor is the closed-form Einstein midpoint a_i = sum_j w_ij*gamma_j*p_j / ||sum_j w_ij*gamma_j*p_j||, gamma_j = 1/(1-c||p_j||^2), and a_1^i = log_0(a_i). Greedy loop l = 1..L: atilde_l = a_l * min(1, ||r_l||/||a_l||); score_k = d_c(exp_0(r_l), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0(atilde_l), e_{l,k})^2; take the argmin, emit SID_i[l] = k, set u = log_0(e_{l,k}), then r_{l+1} = r_l - u and a_{l+1} = a_l - u. Loss = mean_i d_c(p_i, exp_0(sum_l u_{l,c_l}))^2 plus the baseline commitment term; codebook update rule unchanged. Both score terms carry weight 1 by unit symmetry, the anchor clip ratio is 1, k = 20 is a documented default (twice the Recall@10 cut-off) and only positive PMI is admitted, so no constant is swept.

ideas.title: Popularity-adjusted neighbour anchors steer a curved RQ-VAE residual: a behaviour-conditioned Poincare code selection that constrains every SID prefix level

objective: Improve the item semantic IDs of a generative recommender: a training-only behaviour signal must guide the whole SID prefix hierarchy in a hyperbolic RQ-VAE, and the result must raise the Stage 3 test recall above 0.065.
